stem: When we see an image with missing parts, our brain fills in the blanks so we still recognise the pattern. Which Gestalt principle is this?
explanation: The principle of closure says we look for a single recognisable pattern and fill in missing parts; it is often used in logo design.

stem: Which theory of visual perception says we do not perceive the world directly, but process an image before it is consciously recognised, helped by context?
explanation: Constructivism holds that we process images before recognising them and that contextual information helps, which is why the same '-' symbol can mean different things in different contexts.

stem: According to the lecture, which sense is the most dominant in how humans perceive information?
explanation: Vision is the most dominant sense, followed by hearing and touch, so information should be presented so it is readily perceived as intended.

stem: Experiential cognition requires mental effort, as in writing.
explanation: Experiential cognition is intuitive and effortless, as in eating; reflective cognition is the one that requires mental effort, as in writing.

stem: The law of proximity states that elements placed close to each other are perceived as belonging together.
explanation: Proximity is why websites set related content close together and restaurant menus group items such as desserts together.

stem: Which of these are among the five major human senses listed in the lecture? Select all that apply.
explanation: The five major senses listed are sight, hearing, touch, taste and smell.

stem: Studying cognitive psychology helps designers know how humans do which of the following? Select all that apply.
explanation: Cognitive psychology helps designers understand how humans process information, perceive the world, focus attention and use memory, so systems can match their capabilities and limitations.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 6, slide 'Why study cognitive psychology?'; CSC 531 2023/24 past question 1(c)

stem: Which of these are variations of the Gestalt principles listed in the lecture? Select all that apply.
explanation: The variations listed are common region, proximity, figure-ground, similarity, closure, focal point and continuity; affordance is a design principle.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 6, slide 'Gestalt Principle' (Variations); HCI 2020-21 past question 2(b)

stem: Three of these are cognitive processes listed in the lecture. Which is the odd one out?
explanation: Cognitive processes include attention, perception, memory, learning, language, and problem solving; triangulation is a data gathering concept.

stem: Three of these statements describe the ecological theory of perception. Which is the odd one out?

options.text: It lets us recognise objects even when parts of them are obscured
It relies on world knowledge to make sense of what we see
We process any image before it is consciously recognised
Information is extracted directly from the light captured by the eye

explanation: Processing an image before conscious recognition is the constructivist view; the ecological view uses world knowledge and extracts information directly from light.
source: CSC 531 Lecture 6, slides 'Visual Perception' and 'Visual Perception: Ecological'
